greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. We gather today in the presence of the Lord, seeking the light of His Word to guide our hearts through the quiet spaces of our lives.
penitential:
Lord, have mercy.
Christ, have mercy.
Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob.
homily:
We begin today with a very small, very ordinary thing: a hand-written letter. Think of it. St. Paul, an old man, sitting in the cold, damp dark of a prison cell, taking up a pen. He isn't writing a theological treatise or a grand decree. He is writing to a friend, Philemon, about a young man named Onesimus. He calls this boy his own heart. He tells Philemon, 'I am sending him, that is, my own heart, back to you.'

I want you to hold onto this image: the heart being carried in a letter. It is the image of a love that refuses to be contained by distance, by prison walls, or even by the boundary between this life and the next. It is the image of a connection so profound that it becomes a part of the very person who carries it. It is the image of Benjamin Vo.

Let us tell the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who hold the memory of Benjamin as a sacred trust: it has been four months since he went home to God. We know the reality of your quiet house. We know the moments when the silence becomes a weight, when the habits of a lifetime—the brilliant, curious mind that loved to explore the architecture of the world, the gentle, respectful spirit that made him such a treasure—are suddenly interrupted by the sharp, cold realization that he is not there in the way he once was. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that is heavy, real, and unrelenting. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to feel the sudden ache when a memory ambushes you in the middle of an ordinary Tuesday. Do not pretend the weight is lighter than it is.

And let us gently lift one particular stone from your hearts today—a stone that grief often slips into our pockets without us noticing. Sometimes, when a family suffers an unimaginable loss, the mind begins to circle back, whispering quiet, unfair questions. Did we miss a sign? Could we have done something more? Could we have watched closer? Let us lay that burden down right here at the altar. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of a lifetime—traveling the globe together, sharing quiet stories, and walking side by side. You were the exact parents and the exact brother that Benjamin needed. Let that heavy stone fall; you are absolved, and you are held. You did not fail him in any way. You were the light in his life, just as he was the light in yours. Some things in this life are simply beyond our control, and God does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of the cross. You are held in His mercy, not judged by your sorrow.

Now, let the Gospel break into that quiet room. Jesus says, 'The coming of the Kingdom of God cannot be observed, and no one will announce, “Look, here it is,” or, “There it is.” For behold, the Kingdom of God is among you.' The Pharisees were looking for a sign in the sky, a spectacle, something they could pin down. But Jesus points inward, toward the presence of the Father that is already here, hidden in the fabric of the ordinary. Benjamin understood this. Think of his brilliant, searching mind—the way he mastered mathematics, the way he coded those games on GitHub, or how he would talk about his ‘con chim airlines’ with such a genuine, infectious giggle. He wasn't trying to build an empire for the world to see; he was trying to build a connection, a way to share his joy with those he loved. That is the boy you raised. That is the boy who is now at the banquet of heaven, interceding for you. He is not a memory; he is a living soul, fully alive in the love of God. He has found the destination he was searching for, and he is waiting for the rest of his family to arrive.

Consider the first reading from St. Paul to Philemon again: 'Perhaps this is why he was away from you for a while, that you might have him back forever, no longer as a slave but more than a slave, a brother.' Paul is speaking of a transformation. He is speaking of a bond that is no longer defined by the limitations of the earth, but by the eternal life of the Lord. Benjamin’s life was a testament to this grace. Think of that remarkable moment when he unprompted told his parents that he was willing to give up his entire piggy bank to help his uncle William, who was suffering. He didn't need to break it open; the offer itself revealed the magnificent generosity of his soul. He was a boy whose heart was already sized for eternity. He was a boy who knew that the true wealth of life is not what we keep, but what we are willing to offer for the sake of those we love. That love is still flowing. It flows in the well dedicated in his name, it flows in the meals shared in his honor, and it flows in the kindness you show to one another every single day. He was a servant of love, and he is still serving you from the other side.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the games you coded, the dreams you shared, the simple, everyday life of being brothers. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Your brother's love is not gone; it is woven into the very fabric of who you are becoming.

We hear in the Psalm: 'The LORD gives sight to the blind. The LORD raises up those who were bowed down; the LORD loves the just.' This is the turn of the heart. The salvation of the just is not a reward for our labor; it is a gift of God’s presence. We do not work to earn heaven; we work because we are already loved. We serve because we have already been served by the One who washed our feet. Benjamin is now resting in that security. He is dwelling in the land of the living, and he is watching over you with a love that has been purified and perfected in the sight of God.

Think of the dream you had, Alan. You were waiting in line to buy ice cream, and Ben paid. That is the image of the kingdom. It is the image of the one who has gone before us, the one who is now in the position of the steward of grace, waiting to welcome you. He is not distant. He is not gone. He is simply ahead, preparing the way. He is the one who will one day stand at the door of the Father’s house and say, 'I am here, and my family is with me.' That dream was a whisper from heaven. It was a reminder that the bond you share is not broken by death. It is only changed, deepened, and held in the eternal keeping of God. He is well, he is strong, and he is watching over you with a love that has been purified and perfected in the sight of God.

There is a peace that comes from knowing that we are held. It is not a peace that takes away the pain, but it is a peace that keeps us from being destroyed by it. It is the peace of knowing that Benjamin is waiting. He is waiting in the light, he is waiting in the place where there is no more struggling, no more darkness, only the clear, bright presence of the Father. He is waiting for you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is the sign that the work is going well. That smile is the promise that the reunion is certain. He is a light in the world, and he is shining for you. He is the one who has already passed the test, as he said in your dream: 'Ba ơi, test nào con cũng qua hết.' He is home. And because he is home, you are never truly lost.

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Breathe in. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin standing beside you, smiling that bright, cheeky grin, looking out toward an endless horizon. Let yourself be gathered into the peace of Christ. Walk out knowing that you are loved, that you are not to blame, and that the one who went before you is waiting at the door of eternity, holding the key. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may His face shine upon you and bring you peace. Go in the love of the Father.
standing_petitions: For a boy named Ben and all who have died, that they rest in the light of Christ.
For all who grieve, that God console them and give them hope.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Beloved:
I have experienced much joy and encouragement from your love,
because the hearts of the holy ones
have been refreshed by you, brother.
Therefore, although I have the full right in Christ
to order you to do what is proper,
I rather urge you out of love,
being as I am, Paul, an old man,
and now also a prisoner for Christ Jesus.
I urge you on behalf of my child Onesimus,
whose father I have become in my imprisonment,
who was once useless to you but is now useful to both you and me.
I am sending him, that is, my own heart, back to you.
I should have liked to retain him for myself,
so that he might serve me on your behalf
in my imprisonment for the Gospel,
but I did not want to do anything without your consent,
so that the good you do might not be forced but voluntary.
Perhaps this is why he was away from you for a while,
that you might have him back forever,
no longer as a slave but more than a slave, a brother,
beloved especially to me, but even more so to you,
as a man and in the Lord.
So if you regard me as a partner, welcome him as you would me.
And if he has done you any injustice
or owes you anything, charge it to me.
I, Paul, write this in my own hand: I will pay.
May I not tell you that you owe me your very self.
Yes, brother, may I profit from you in the Lord.
Refresh my heart in Christ.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (5a) Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob.
or:
R. Alleluia.
The LORD secures justice for the oppressed,
gives food to the hungry.
The LORD sets captives free.
R. Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob.
or:
R. Alleluia.
The LORD gives sight to the blind.
The LORD raises up those who were bowed down;
the LORD loves the just.
The LORD protects strangers.
R. Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob.
or:
R. Alleluia.
The fatherless and the widow he sustains,
but the way of the wicked he thwarts.
The LORD shall reign forever;
your God, O Zion, through all generations. Alleluia.
R. Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob.
or:
R. Alleluia.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Asked by the Pharisees when the Kingdom of God would come,
Jesus said in reply,
“The coming of the Kingdom of God cannot be observed,
and no one will announce, ‘Look, here it is,’ or, ‘There it is.’
For behold, the Kingdom of God is among you.”Then he said to his disciples,
“The days will come when you will long to see
one of the days of the Son of Man, but you will not see it.
There will be those who will say to you,
‘Look, there he is,’ or ‘Look, here he is.’
Do not go off, do not run in pursuit.
For just as lightning flashes
and lights up the sky from one side to the other,
so will the Son of Man be in his day.
But first he must suffer greatly and be rejected by this generation.”

Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
